q: What is the DAEDS Recommended Professional Fee (RPF)?
scenario: An architect is engaged for the Regular Design Services of a Group III (Exceptional) project — a regional stadium (stadia) complex — with a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of P700,000,000.

q: A developer is planning a resort with a marina component and wants to know if it qualifies for the higher Group III fee rates instead of ordinary Group I rates. What should the architect confirm before applying Group III rates?
o: That the project is a marina and/or resort complex, which SPP Document 202 explicitly lists under Group III (Exceptional)
That the project is located within Metro Manila
That the total floor area exceeds 10,000 square meters
That the client has hired a structural engineer
n: Marinas and Resort Complexes are explicitly named under Group 3 in Sec. 6.3.3; classification is based on the building type matching the enumerated list, not on floor area, engineering staffing, or location. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.3)

q: SPP Document 202 gives a Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) schedule for Group III expressed for two kinds of engagement. What do the abbreviations DAEDS and DADS stand for?
o: Detailed Assessment of Engineering Design Standards, and Development of Architectural Design Specifications
Detailed Architectural Estimation and Drafting Services, and Design Approval and Documentation Services
Design and Engineering Documentation Services, and Design and Development Services
Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services, and Detailed Architectural Design Services
n: DAEDS is Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services (the architect provides both architectural and full engineering design), while DADS is Detailed Architectural Design Services only. Sec. 6.3.3 gives separate RPF schedules for each. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.3)

q: The Group III (Exceptional) fee schedule and the Group III building list both appear under which subsection of the Regular Design Services guidelines in SPP Document 202?
n: Sec. 6.3.3 of SPP Document 202 sets out both the Group 3 building type list and its DAEDS/DADS Recommended Professional Fee bracket schedules. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.3)

q: What is the DAEDS Recommended Professional Fee (RPF)?
n: PCC = P40M falls in the 'P50.0 million and less' bracket, where DAEDS RPF = 7% of PCC = 0.07 x 40,000,000 = P2,800,000.00. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.3)
scenario: An architect is engaged for the Regular Design Services of a Group III (Exceptional) project — a public health center — with a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of P40,000,000.

q: What is the DADS Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) for the same project?
scenario: An architect is engaged for the Regular Design Services of a Group III (Exceptional) project — a major transportation hub — with a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of P1,500,000,000 (P1.5 billion).

q: Which bracket of the Group III RPF schedule applies, and what is the DAEDS RPF?
o: The 'P50.0 million and less' bracket applies; RPF = 6% x 50,000,000 = P3,000,000.00
The 'Over P50.0 million to P100.0 million' bracket applies; RPF = P3,500,000 + 6% of excess of P50M
The 'P50.0 million and less' bracket applies; RPF = 7% x 50,000,000 = P3,500,000.00
The 'Over P100.0 million to P200.0 million' bracket applies; RPF = P6,500,000 + 5% of excess of P100M
n: PCC = P50M falls exactly at the top of the 'P50.0 million and less' bracket, so DAEDS RPF = 7% x 50,000,000 = P3,500,000.00 (which also equals the base amount that begins the next bracket's formula, P3,500,000 + 6% of excess of P50M). (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.3)
scenario: An architect is engaged for the Regular Design Services of a Group III (Exceptional) project — a gymnasium complex — with a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of exactly P50,000,000.

q: What is the DADS Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) for the same project?
n: PCC = P80M falls in the 'Over P50.0 million to P100.0 million' bracket: RPF = P2,100,000 + 3.6% of excess of P50M = 2,100,000 + [0.036 x (80,000,000 - 50,000,000)] = 2,100,000 + 1,080,000 = P3,180,000.00. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.3)
scenario: An architect is engaged for the Regular Design Services of a Group III (Exceptional) project with a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of P80,000,000.

q: What is the DADS Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) for the same project?
scenario: An architect is engaged for the Regular Design Services of a Group III (Exceptional) project — an international airport terminal — with a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of P350,000,000.

q: What fundamentally distinguishes Group III buildings under SPP Document 202's Regular Design Services fee schedule?
o: They are monumental buildings requiring consummate design skill and much precise detailing
They are buildings of exceptional character and complexity of plan/design, or requiring comparatively large amounts of research and of engineering and allied architectural design
They are ordinary residences, small apartment houses, and townhouses
They are simple structures needing only a minimum of architectural finishes, engineering, and allied architectural elements
n: SPP 202, Sec. 6.3.3 defines Group 3 as buildings of exceptional character and complexity of plan/design, or requiring comparatively large amounts of research and of engineering and allied architectural design — distinct from Group I (simple, Sec. 6.3.1), Group IV (residences, Sec. 6.3.4-6.3.5... actually Group 4), and Group V (monumental buildings). (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.3)

q: How does the Group III DADS base-bracket rate (PCC of P50.0 million and less) of 4.2% compare to the Group III DAEDS base-bracket rate of 7% for the same PCC range?
o: DADS is higher than DAEDS because architectural-only work is more time-intensive
DADS is exactly 60% of the DAEDS rate
DADS and DAEDS are the same because both cover identical scopes of work
DADS is not defined for the base bracket
n: 4.2% / 7% = 0.6, so the Group III DADS base rate is exactly 60% of the DAEDS base rate, reflecting that DADS compensates architectural design services alone while DAEDS compensates architectural plus engineering design services combined, per Sec. 6.3.3. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.3)

q: An architect completes DAEDS for a Group III telecommunications building with PCC = P120,000,000. The client later asks the architect to also justify why the fee percentage (5% base of the excess) is lower than the 6% rate used for a P80M-PCC Group III project earlier that year. What is the best explanation?
o: The Group III RPF schedule is a bracketed/graduated schedule where the percentage applied to the excess amount decreases as the PCC bracket increases
The 6% rate was a billing error and should have been 5%
Telecommunication buildings are always billed at a discount
DAEDS rates only apply to hospitals, not telecommunication buildings
n: The Group III RPF schedule under Sec. 6.3.3 is graduated: 7% (<=50M), 6% (50-100M), 5% (100-200M), 4% (200-500M), 3% (500M-1B), 2% (over 1B) for DAEDS — the marginal percentage decreases as the PCC bracket rises, which is normal and not an error. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.3)

q: What is the DAEDS Recommended Professional Fee (RPF)?
scenario: An architect is engaged for the Regular Design Services of a Group III (Exceptional) project — a major transportation hub — with a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of P1,500,000,000 (P1.5 billion).

q: A hospital and medical center project is being classified for fee purposes under SPP Document 202. Which building type group applies?
n: Hospitals & Medical Buildings are explicitly listed under Group 3 (Exceptional) in Sec. 6.3.3, together with other buildings requiring exceptional design complexity and research. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.3)

q: An architect designed a mortuary and, separately, a veterinary hospital in the same year. A junior staff member assumes these should be billed under two different building type groups since they serve very different purposes. Is this assumption correct?
o: No, both Mortuaries and Veterinary Hospitals are listed under Group III (Exceptional), so both use the same RPF schedule
No, both are classified under Group VII (Housing Projects)
Yes, mortuaries are Group V and veterinary hospitals are Group III
Yes, mortuaries are Group I and veterinary hospitals are Group IV
n: Both Mortuaries and Veterinary Hospitals are explicitly listed under Group 3 (Exceptional) in Sec. 6.3.3, so both projects would use the same Group III RPF schedule despite serving very different purposes. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.3)

q: An architect is asked to design a nuclear power research facility with a construction cost of P600 million, and the client wants the architect to handle both architectural design and the full engineering design (structural, electrical, mechanical, etc.). Under SPP Document 202, which fee schedule and bracket should the architect apply?
o: Group IV DAEDS schedule, flat 10% of PCC
Group III DADS schedule, 'Over P500.0 million to P1.0 billion' bracket
Group I DAEDS schedule, 'P50.0 million and less' bracket
Group III DAEDS schedule, 'Over P500.0 million to P1.0 billion' bracket
n: Nuclear facilities are Group III (Exceptional) buildings under Sec. 6.3.3. Because the architect is rendering both architectural and engineering design services, the DAEDS schedule applies, and a P600M PCC falls in the 'Over P500.0 million to P1.0 billion' bracket. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.3)

q: A veterinary hospital, a mortuary, and a mental institution are being classified under SPP Document 202's building type groups for Regular Design Services. Under which group do all three fall?
n: Veterinary Hospitals, Mortuaries, and Mental Institutions are all explicitly enumerated under Group 3 (Exceptional) in Sec. 6.3.3. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.3)

q: What is the DADS Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) for the same project?
n: PCC = P40M falls in the 'P50.0 million and less' bracket, where DADS RPF = 4.2% of PCC = 0.042 x 40,000,000 = P1,680,000.00. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.3)
scenario: An architect is engaged for the Regular Design Services of a Group III (Exceptional) project — a public health center — with a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of P40,000,000.

q: Which of the following best summarizes what a candidate should know about Group III under SPP Document 202 for the AR licensure exam: its scope, its RPF basis, and its two service-scope variants?
o: Group III applies only to alteration and renovation work, distinct from new design
Group III covers only residential buildings, uses a flat 10% RPF, and has no DAEDS/DADS distinction
Group III covers monumental buildings only and uses a flat 12% RPF with no bracket structure

Group III covers buildings of exceptional character/complexity (e.g., hospitals, airports, stadia, laboratories) requiring large amounts of research, uses a graduated percent-of-PCC RPF bracket schedule (Sec. 6.3.3), and provides separate DAEDS (architectural + engineering) and DADS (architectural only) fee schedules
n: Group III (Exceptional) under Sec. 6.3.3 covers buildings such as hospitals, airports, stadia, and laboratories that require exceptional design complexity or large amounts of research; its RPF is computed on a graduated percent-of-PCC bracket schedule, with separate DAEDS and DADS versions of the schedule. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.3)

q: Which building classification group under SPP Document 202's Regular Design Services schedule is labeled 'Exceptional' and covers structures such as hospitals, airports, and research facilities?
n: Group III is the 'Exceptional' classification, covering buildings of exceptional character/complexity or requiring large amounts of research and engineering and allied architectural design — including hospitals, airports, and research facilities. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.3)

q: What is the DAEDS Recommended Professional Fee (RPF)?
n: PCC = P150M falls in the 'Over P100.0 million to P200.0 million' bracket: RPF = P6,500,000 + 5% of excess of P100M = 6,500,000 + [0.05 x (150,000,000 - 100,000,000)] = 6,500,000 + 2,500,000 = P9,000,000.00. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.3)
scenario: An architect is engaged for the Regular Design Services of a Group III (Exceptional) project — a convention center — with a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of P150,000,000.

q: A brewery, a cold storage facility, a hotel, a medical arts office/clinic, and a theater are each being classified for Regular Design Services fee purposes under SPP Document 202. Under which single group do ALL five of these building types fall?
o: They are split across four different groups
n: Breweries, Cold Storage Facilities, Hotels, Medical Arts Offices & Clinics, and Theaters & Similar Facilities are all explicitly enumerated under Group 3 (Exceptional) in Sec. 6.3.3, so a single Group III RPF schedule applies to all five. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.3)

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the building types listed under Group III (Exceptional) of SPP Document 202?
n: Habitable Agricultural Buildings are listed under Group I (Simple). Convention Facilities, Marinas and Resort Complexes, and Auditoriums are all Group 3 building types per Sec. 6.3.3. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.3)

q: In the Group III Recommended Professional Fee schedule, what happens to the percentage rate applied to the 'excess' portion of the Project Construction Cost as the PCC bracket increases from 'P50.0 million and less' up to 'Over P1.0 billion' (DAEDS case)?
o: It stays constant at 7% throughout all brackets
It increases steadily from 7% up to a maximum of 12%
n: The Group III DAEDS schedule under Sec. 6.3.3 is a graduated/regressive schedule: 7% (<=50M), 6% (50-100M), 5% (100-200M), 4% (200-500M), 3% (500M-1B), and 2% (over 1B) applied to the excess over each bracket's floor. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.3)

q: Within Group III's Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) schedule, why is the DADS (Detailed Architectural Design Services) percentage-of-PCC rate lower than the DAEDS (Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services) rate at every bracket?
o: DADS covers architectural design services alone, without the allied engineering design services bundled into DAEDS
DADS and DAEDS rates are actually identical for Group III
DADS is charged only on projects below P50 million
DADS applies only to Group I buildings
n: DADS compensates the architect for architectural design services only, while DAEDS compensates for both architectural and the allied engineering design services, so the DAEDS percentage is consistently higher (e.g., 7% vs. 4.2% at the base bracket) under Sec. 6.3.3. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.3)

q: An architect is asked whether a proposed 'exceptional' classification and its higher fee percentages can be applied to a simple two-story service garage just because the client wants a higher fee. What should the architect do?
o: Classify the project according to its actual building type under the SPP list — a service garage is Group I (Simple), not Group III, regardless of the fee the client is willing to pay
Apply Group III rates if the client requests it, since client preference governs classification
Refuse to take any fee under SPP Document 202
Split the difference and average Group I and Group III rates
n: Classification under SPP Document 202 is based on the building type's actual character per Sec. 6.3.1-6.3.3, not on client preference for a higher fee; service garages are explicitly Group I (Simple). (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.3)

q: Relative to Group I (Simple) buildings, how do Group III (Exceptional) buildings' base DAEDS Recommended Professional Fee percentages compare?
o: Group III shares the same 7% base rate as Group I at the lowest PCC bracket, reflecting that both groups' base bracket carries the schedule's higher-end starting rate for their respective category
Group III has no defined fee schedule at all
Group III's percentages are lower than Group I's because exceptional buildings need less oversight
Group III's percentages are identical to Group I's at every bracket
n: Both Group I and Group III use 7% as the DAEDS base-bracket rate (PCC <=50M) in their respective schedules — however, the overall design and coordination burden implied by 'exceptional character and complexity' is what justifies Group III's separate classification. Sec. 6.3.1 (Group I) and Sec. 6.3.3 (Group III) each set out their own bracket schedules. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.3)

q: A project involves an existing airport terminal (Group III) that will undergo not new construction but extensive alteration and renovation. Should the architect still use the Group III Regular Design Services fee brackets described in Sec. 6.3.3?
o: No — SPP Document 202 provides a separate group/schedule specifically for alterations, renovations, rehabilitation, retrofit, and expansion/addition work (Group IX), distinct from the regular new-design Group III schedule
Yes, because airports are always Group III regardless of scope of work
No, alteration work is not covered anywhere in SPP Document 202
Yes, alterations always use the same fee schedule as new construction
n: SPP Document 202 separately classifies Alterations, Renovations, Rehabilitations, Retrofit, and Expansion/Addition work under its own group (Group IX), distinct from the Group III new-design brackets, since the nature and effort of alteration work differs from new design. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.3)

q: Laboratories/Testing Facilities and Research Facilities are both classified under which SPP Document 202 building type group, consistent with the group's rationale of requiring large amounts of research?
n: Both Laboratories/Testing Facilities and Research Facilities are Group 3 buildings; the group's defining rationale in Sec. 6.3.3 explicitly includes buildings 'requiring comparatively large amounts of research and of engineering and allied architectural design.' (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.3)

q: What is the overall purpose of the building type group classifications (Group I through Group X) found in SPP Document 202's Regular Design Services fee guidelines?
o: To determine which architects are licensed to practice
To regulate the construction materials used in each building type
To categorize projects by design complexity/character so that an appropriate Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) percentage-of-PCC schedule can be applied
n: The Group I-X classification system in SPP Document 202 exists to categorize projects by their design complexity and character so that the correct RPF percentage-of-PCC bracket schedule is applied — simpler buildings (Group I) get lower base percentages, while more complex ones (e.g., Group III, V) get higher ones. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.3)

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the building types listed under Group III (Exceptional) of SPP Document 202?
n: Public Markets are listed under Group I (Simple), not Group III. Stadia, Telecommunication Buildings, and Observatories are all Group III (Exceptional) building types under Sec. 6.3.3. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.3)

q: A client engages an architect solely to prepare the architectural design (not the engineering design, which will be handled by separate engineering consultants) for a new public hospital. Which Group III fee schedule should the architect use to compute the Recommended Professional Fee?
n: When the architect renders architectural design services only (engineering design handled separately), the DADS (Detailed Architectural Design Services) schedule applies, not DAEDS, which is for combined architectural-and-engineering design. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.3)

q: Which pair of building types are BOTH explicitly listed under Group III (Exceptional) of SPP Document 202?
o: Airports/Wet & Dry Ports & Terminals and Nuclear Facilities
n: Airports/Wet & Dry Ports & Terminals and Nuclear Facilities are both listed under Group 3 in Sec. 6.3.3. Warehouses/Service Garages are Group I (Simple); row-houses/townhouses are Group IV (Residences); Museums/Mausoleums are Group V (Monumental). (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.3)

q: An architect is designing a private aquarium and marine research center. A colleague argues this should be classified as Group I because it is a single-purpose commercial building. Is the colleague correct?
o: No, aquariums are Group V monumental buildings
Yes, because aquariums do not require engineering design
No, Aquariums are explicitly listed as a Group III (Exceptional) building type under SPP Document 202
Yes, all single-purpose commercial buildings are Group I
n: Aquariums are explicitly enumerated under Group 3 (Exceptional) in Sec. 6.3.3, not Group I. Classification follows the building type list in the SPP, not a general commercial/single-purpose label. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.3)
